idea.body: A complex number a + bi has a real part a and an imaginary part b, where i is defined so that i^2 = -1. Adding or subtracting complex numbers combines the real parts together and the imaginary parts together. Multiplying works like multiplying two binomials, using i^2 = -1 to simplify. Every complex number a + bi has a conjugate, a - bi. A number times its own conjugate always gives a real number, a^2 + b^2. This matters for quadratics: when the discriminant is negative, the two roots are a conjugate pair, p + qi and p - qi. Every quadratic has two roots once complex numbers are allowed. A complex number can be plotted as a point, real part on the horizontal axis and imaginary part on the vertical axis.

figure.alt: The point (3, 4) in the complex plane, representing 3 + 4i.

steps: Use the quadratic formula: x = (2 +/- sqrt(4 - 20))/2.
The discriminant is 4 - 20, which is -16, a negative number.
sqrt(-16) is sqrt(16) times i, which is 4i.
x = (2 +/- 4i)/2, which simplifies to 1 +/- 2i.
The two roots are 1 + 2i and 1 - 2i, a conjugate pair.

figure.alt: The two roots 1 + 2i and 1 - 2i plotted as points in the complex plane.

ways.name: The rules of i as a cycle
ways.when: when you need a high power of i, like i^25 or i^100.
steps: Remember: i^1 = i, i^2 = -1, i^3 = -i, i^4 = 1.
The pattern repeats every 4.
Divide the exponent by 4 and find the remainder.
Match the remainder to the pattern above.
ways.answer: 17 divided by 4 is 4 remainder 1, so i^17 = i^1 = i
ways.trap: Forgetting that i^2 = -1, not 1, and getting the cycle wrong.

ways.name: Multiply like binomials then apply i^2 = -1
ways.when: when you multiply two complex numbers a + bi by c + di.
steps: Expand (a + bi)(c + di) like you would (a + b)(c + d).
Collect real and imaginary parts: ac, ad i, bc i, bd i^2.
Replace i^2 with -1: bd i^2 becomes -bd.
Combine: (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i.
ways.trap: Forgetting to replace i^2 with -1 and getting an extra i in your answer.

ways.name: The conjugate trick
ways.when: when you divide by a complex number or need to eliminate i from a denominator.
steps: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi.
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate.
The denominator becomes (a + bi)(a - bi) = a^2 + b^2, which is real.
The numerator expands and simplifies with the conjugate.
ways.trap: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the wrong conjugate, or forgetting the factor.

ways.name: The plane picture
ways.when: when you visualize complex numbers as points on a coordinate grid.
steps: The horizontal axis is the real part.
The vertical axis is the imaginary part.
Plot a + bi as the point (a, b).
Distance from the origin is the modulus: sqrt(a^2 + b^2).
ways.trap: Confusing the real and imaginary axes, or forgetting the modulus formula.

figure.alt: The complex plane with 3 + 4i plotted at (3, 4) and the segment from the origin, whose length is the modulus 5.
